newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soldier kills 3 colleagues in shooting spree.
newsitem.headline: Indian soldier kills 3 colleagues in shooting spree.

text.p: An Indian army soldier ran amok with a gun and shot dead three of his colleagues and wounded another in the troubled state of Jammu and Kashmir, a defence spokesman said on Wednesday.
"A soldier of Rashtriya Rifles on Tuesday night ran amok in Budgam army camp and shot dead three of his colleagues and wounded another," said Major P. Purushottam, an Indian defence spokesman.
Budgam town lies 15 km (nine miles) southwest of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
This is the third major incident in the Himalayan region in which soldiers have been killed by colleagues since a nerve-racking Moslem guerrilla rebellion broke out in 1990.
The Rashtriya Rifles, a wing of the Indian army, is engaged in fighting separatists in the state, largely Hindu India's only Moslem majority province.
In July an Indian soldier killed five colleagues, including two officers, in Shopian army camp, 50 km (31 miles) south of Srinagar.
Last December, a Rashtriya Rifles soldier killed five colleagues and wounded seven others in a similar incident in Srinagar.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed since the separatist revolt began. Separatist groups and the state's chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, put the toll near 50,000.
